contents.html:
Sub-process IDD.2
Sub-process nameIdentify System Functions and Capabilities Workflow Needed and What Components/Subcomponents Will be Used
Sub-process descriptionThis sub-process analyzes the system to identify the components and subcomponents required to ensure that the system functions as intended.

Review the activities identified in D.1. For existing systems, list the functions and capabilities of the system being analyzed. For systems under development, list functions and capabilities needed. If the system is complex, consider scoping the analysis to only the functions and capabilities determined as critical. Consider configurations, settings, routines, performance parameters, etc.

Define the processes or data actions that are activated or that the system uses to perform the identified functions and capabilities. Those processes can be extracted from existing system documentation, such as functional requirements, system diagrams, process flow diagrams, system concept of operations, or any other documentation that describes what the system does. Consider defining what information/data is needed to perform a function: how will that data be processed and how it will be secured.

Finally, identify components and subcomponents that are or will be used to support required functionalities and capabilities. If possible, define all of the functions and capabilities of those components and subcomponents; identify which functions or capabilities are not needed or outside the requirements for this particular application. For example, configuration settings or functions that will not be used. Consider the frequency of use of subsystem functions and capabilities and describing end-of-life conditions, such as when the functions/capabilities are expected to no longer be needed, for the system to function.
InputsDetermination of the system/subsystem from D.1; Existing documentation, system design process, architecture diagrams; existing contractual obligations
OutputsListing of capabilities and pathways needed to pass to D.3.
MethodsDocument Review; Process Analysis; Systems Analysis; Workflow Analysis; Data Flow Diagrams; Functional Decomposition; Interface Analysis

contents.html_ja:
サブプロセス IDD.2
サブプロセス名必要なシステム機能と能力、および使用するコンポーネント／サブコンポーネントの特定
サブプロセスの説明このサブプロセスは、システムが意図したとおりに機能することを確実にするために必要なコンポーネントとサブコンポーネントを特定するために、システムを分析します。

D.1 で特定した活動をレビューしてください。既存のシステムの場合は、分析対象のシステムの機能と能力を一覧にしてください。開発中のシステムの場合は、必要な機能と能力を一覧にしてください。システムが複雑な場合は、重要と判断された機能と能力のみに分析のスコープを絞ることを検討してください。構成、設定、ルーチン、性能パラメータなどを検討してください。

特定した機能と能力を実行するために起動される、またはシステムが使用するプロセスやデータ操作を定義してください。これらのプロセスは、機能要件、システム図、プロセスフロー図、システムの運用コンセプト、またはシステムが何をするかを記述するその他の文書など、既存のシステム文書から抽出できます。機能を実行するためにどのような情報／データが必要か、そのデータをどのように処理し、どのように保護するかを定義することを検討してください。

最後に、必要な機能と能力を支えるために使われている、または使われる予定のコンポーネントとサブコンポーネントを特定してください。可能であれば、それらのコンポーネントとサブコンポーネントのすべての機能と能力を定義し、どの機能や能力が不要であるか、またはこの特定の用途の要件の範囲外であるかを特定してください。たとえば、使用されない構成設定や機能があります。サブシステムの機能と能力の使用頻度を検討し、システムが機能するうえで、それらの機能／能力がいつ不要になると想定されるかといった、寿命終了時の条件を記述することを検討してください。
入力D.1 のシステム／サブシステムの決定、既存の文書、システム設計プロセス、アーキテクチャ図、既存の契約上の義務
出力D.3 に渡す、必要な能力と経路の一覧。
方法文書レビュー、プロセス分析、システム分析、ワークフロー分析、データフロー図、機能分解、インタフェース分析

contents.html:
Sub-process IDD.3
Sub-process nameIdentify Interactions, Intersections, Connections, and Dependencies Within the System(s)/Subsystem(s)
Sub-process descriptionThis sub-process identifies interactions, intersections, connections, and dependencies between components/subcomponents and associated functionalities/capabilities.

The way the system uses components and subcomponents to execute a specific function or capability is described as a workflow path. Defined workflow paths may be extremely detailed, including the individual processes used by subcomponents. Note that detailed workflow paths allow for a more accurate and complete criticality analysis, but may not be feasible in many instances.

Identify all workflow paths required to execute each system function or, if the system is complex, each critical function. In many cases, a single component, or identical components, will be used to support multiple workflow paths. Document these components matched to workflow paths in a matrix, spreadsheet, database, function diagram, or a similar tool.

Identify interactions, intersections, connections, and dependencies between the components. Identify any constraints within the existing infrastructure. Consider identifying the amount of control the organization has over certain dependencies and constraints (e.g., weather). Consider defining triggers or conditions which activate/deactivate the use of a component or which impact how a component is used.
InputsListing of capabilities and pathways from D.2.

Existing documentation, system design, lists of components, bill of materials, or other documentation that somehow describes components and subcomponents.
OutputsListing of components and subcomponents matched to workflow paths to pass to D.4 and D.5; Function Diagram with Workflow Paths
MethodsDocument Review; Systems Analysis; Brainstorming; Sensitivity/Uncertainty Analysis

サブプロセス IDD.3
サブプロセス名システム／サブシステム内の相互作用、交差、接続、依存関係の特定
サブプロセスの説明このサブプロセスは、コンポーネント／サブコンポーネント間、および関連する機能／能力との間の、相互作用、交差、接続、依存関係を特定します。

システムが特定の機能または能力を実行するためにコンポーネントとサブコンポーネントを使用する方法は、ワークフローパスとして記述されます。定義するワークフローパスは、サブコンポーネントが使用する個別のプロセスを含め、極めて詳細なものになりえます。詳細なワークフローパスは、より正確で完全な重要度分析を可能にしますが、多くの場合は実現が困難な場合があります。

各システム機能、またはシステムが複雑な場合は各重要な機能を実行するために必要なすべてのワークフローパスを特定してください。多くの場合、1 つのコンポーネント、または同一のコンポーネントが、複数のワークフローパスを支えるために使われます。ワークフローパスと対応づけたこれらのコンポーネントを、マトリクス、スプレッドシート、データベース、機能図、または同様のツールに文書化してください。

コンポーネント間の相互作用、交差、接続、依存関係を特定してください。既存のインフラストラクチャ内の制約があれば特定してください。特定の依存関係や制約（たとえば天候）に対して組織がどの程度の制御力を持つかを特定することを検討してください。コンポーネントの使用を有効化／無効化する、またはコンポーネントの使われ方に影響するトリガーや条件を定義することを検討してください。
入力D.2 の能力と経路の一覧。

既存の文書、システム設計、コンポーネントの一覧、部品表、またはコンポーネントとサブコンポーネントを何らかの形で記述するその他の文書。
出力D.4 と D.5 に渡す、ワークフローパスと対応づけたコンポーネントとサブコンポーネントの一覧、ワークフローパスを示す機能図

contents.html:
Sub-process IDD.4
Sub-process nameDefine Operating States
Sub-process descriptionThis sub-process defines normal operational states, as well as the states in which the system will be operating abnormally.

Review the outputs of D.3. Describe operation of the components and/or workflow paths. Then determine the impact of the various operating states of the component on the workflow path(s), and consequently on the system function/capability that path supports. Consider each of the following operating states:

Non-operational;
Impaired (i.e., the component/subcomponent operates at a reduced capability or in an unsafe/insecure/privacy-invasive manner);
Normal operation;
Increased operations (i.e., the function or capability performs quicker or with more output than normal); and
Unintended operations (i.e., the function or capability performs but with additional outputs or actions that are not part of the expected routine).

Consider defining what types of scenarios would lead to such situations. Examples of scenarios to consider include reduced performance (e.g., lower bandwidth), security breach, physical accident, insertion of counterfeit part, or any other similar event.

Using the Function Diagram with Workflow Paths, identify specific points within the workflow paths where the system will be particularly stressed as a result of any of these operating states. This would include any points that would exacerbate the situation.

Define the severity of the impact of the operating states. This may be a ranking (e.g., low, moderate, high) or measure (e.g., processing speed; downtime; percentage of remaining functionality).

Consider the security, safety, and privacy ramifications of these situations; for example, what information is made vulnerable if the components/subcomponents fail? Could the data processing create privacy problems for individuals?

Also consider any contractual, statutory, or other obligations which may be impacted by the operating state.

Consider the lifetime of the component/subcomponent and the duration of an adverse operating state. Often, the impact of an adverse operating state is more severe over a longer time frame.
InputsListing of components and subcomponents matched to workflow paths from D.3; Function Diagram with Workflow Paths
OutputsDescription of operating states to pass to D.5.
MethodsDocument Review; Systems Analysis; Workflow Analysis; Brainstorming; Group Decision Making; Scenario/Use Case

contents.html_ja:
サブプロセス IDD.4
サブプロセス名運用状態の定義
サブプロセスの説明このサブプロセスは、通常の運用状態と、システムが異常に運用される状態を定義します。

D.3 の出力をレビューしてください。コンポーネントまたはワークフローパス（あるいはその両方）の動作を記述してください。次に、コンポーネントのさまざまな運用状態がワークフローパスに及ぼす影響、ひいてはそのパスが支えるシステムの機能／能力に及ぼす影響を判定してください。次の各運用状態を検討してください。

非稼働。
機能低下（すなわち、コンポーネント／サブコンポーネントが低下した能力で、または安全でない／セキュアでない／プライバシーを侵害する方法で動作する）。
通常運用。
運用の増大（すなわち、機能または能力が通常より速く、またはより多くの出力で実行される）。
意図しない運用（すなわち、機能または能力は実行されますが、想定される定常業務に含まれない追加の出力や動作を伴う）。

そうした状況につながるシナリオの種類を定義することを検討してください。検討すべきシナリオの例には、性能の低下（たとえば帯域幅の減少）、セキュリティ侵害、物理的な事故、偽造部品の混入、その他の同様の事象があります。

ワークフローパスを示す機能図を用いて、これらの運用状態のいずれかの結果として、システムに特に負荷がかかるワークフローパス内の具体的な箇所を特定してください。これには、状況を悪化させる箇所も含まれます。

運用状態の影響の深刻度を定義してください。これは、順位付け（たとえば低、中、高）でも、尺度（たとえば処理速度、ダウンタイム、残存する機能の割合）でもかまいません。

これらの状況によるセキュリティ、安全性、プライバシーへの波及を検討してください。たとえば、コンポーネント／サブコンポーネントが故障した場合に、どの情報が脆弱になりますか。データ処理が個人にプライバシー上の問題を生じさせる可能性がありますか。

また、運用状態によって影響を受ける可能性のある契約上、法令上、その他の義務も考慮してください。

コンポーネント／サブコンポーネントの寿命と、悪影響を及ぼす運用状態の継続期間を検討してください。悪影響を及ぼす運用状態の影響は、時間枠が長いほど深刻になることがよくあります。
入力D.3 の、ワークフローパスと対応づけたコンポーネントとサブコンポーネントの一覧、ワークフローパスを示す機能図
出力D.5 に渡す運用状態の記述。

contents.html:
Sub-process IDD.5
Sub-process nameAssign Baseline Criticality Levels to Components/Subcomponents
Sub-process descriptionThis sub-process assigns criticality levels to components and subcomponents identified in D.3 based on the impact of the operating states defined in D.4.

Rank the components and subcomponents in a way that gives the highest ranking to components and subcomponents that are on the critical workflow path, perform vital functions and capabilities, and would be most impacted by adverse operating states.

The user can create a ranking schema that would, for example, rank those activities and workflow paths that are impacted by the highest number of scenarios as “High Criticality” and those that are impacted by the lowest number of scenarios as “Low Criticality.” The user could also use ranges and thresholds to define such rankings.
InputsListing of components and subcomponents matched to workflow paths from D.3; Function Diagram with Workflow Paths; Description of operating states from D.4.
OutputsBaseline Criticality Levels of Component(s)/Subcomponent(s)
MethodsDocument Review; Systems Analysis; Process Flow Analysis; Group Decision Making; Root Cause Analysis; Scenario/Use Case

サブプロセス IDD.5
サブプロセス名コンポーネント／サブコンポーネントへのベースライン重要度レベルの割り当て
サブプロセスの説明このサブプロセスは、D.4 で定義した運用状態の影響に基づいて、D.3 で特定したコンポーネントとサブコンポーネントに重要度レベルを割り当てます。

重要なワークフローパス上にあり、不可欠な機能と能力を果たし、悪影響を及ぼす運用状態の影響を最も受けるコンポーネントとサブコンポーネントに最も高い順位を与える形で、コンポーネントとサブコンポーネントを順位付けしてください。

利用者は、たとえば、最も多くのシナリオの影響を受ける活動とワークフローパスを「高重要度」、最も少ないシナリオの影響を受けるものを「低重要度」と順位付けするような、順位付けの体系を作成できます。利用者は、そうした順位付けを定義するために範囲としきい値を使うこともできます。
入力D.3 の、ワークフローパスと対応づけたコンポーネントとサブコンポーネントの一覧、ワークフローパスを示す機能図、D.4 の運用状態の記述。

contents.html:
ProcessE
Process nameConduct Detailed Review of Criticality for Processes B, C, and D
Process summaryThis is a bottom-up sub-process conducted after Baseline Criticality levels have been defined under Processes B, C and D. It is used to create final criticality levels for Systems/Subsystems and Components/Subcomponents.

This process involves identifying interactions, intersections, connections, and dependencies across Processes B, C, and D. It considers any available risk information, including any existing mitigation strategies, to create a more precise criticality score.
InputsBaseline Criticality for B, C, and D; Existing Documentation; System Design Process; Security Requirements; Functional Requirements; Root Cause Analysis; Hazard Analysis; Risk Assessment (esp. Threat Assessment; Vulnerability Assessment, Impact Analysis, Privacy Risk Assessment)
OutputsCriticality Levels of Programs, Systems/Subsystems, and Component(s)/ Subcomponent(s)
Roles and ResponsibilitiesResponsible: Lead System Architect or a similar role is responsible for the performance of this sub-process. Lead Security Engineer serves as a co-lead for this process.

Accountable: Lead System Engineer should work in partnership with Lead Security or Privacy Engineer and Program Manager to ensure appropriate communication and collaboration across Processes B, C, and D.

Consulted: Individuals who have detailed knowledge of the activities identified by this process should participate in this process to contribute to the identification of critical activities. These individuals may include system architects and designers, system engineers, security or privacy engineers, other security or privacy professionals, acquisition/procurement professionals, business leaders, and others, as appropriate. Identify representatives of each relevant group to participate in this process.

Informed: Individuals responsible for conducting any part of the criticality analysis.

プロセスの概要これは、プロセス B、C、D でベースライン重要度レベルが定義された後に実施される、ボトムアップのサブプロセスです。システム／サブシステムおよびコンポーネント／サブコンポーネントの最終的な重要度レベルを作成するために用いられます。

このプロセスでは、プロセス B、C、D をまたぐ相互作用、交差、接続、依存関係を特定します。既存の緩和戦略を含む利用可能なリスク情報を考慮し、より精密な重要度スコアを作成します。

Sub-process descriptionThis sub-process uses the process diagrams, design documents, or other artifacts created in processes B, C, and D, to trace subcomponents through to program goals and objectives.

One system component or type of system component may be used in multiple subsystems. Identify these by reviewing the system design documentation that was created in Process D for each system or subsystem that was identified in Process C.

Similarly, one system may support multiple programs. Identify these by reviewing the systems identified in Process C for each workflow described in Process B.

Identify identical or similar types of components used for critical functions of multiple systems. Also, identify components or subsystems that originate from a single supplier. Look for any other connection or dependency that may impact the success of the objective or goals if stretched by maintenance, supply chain, security, or other concerns.

contents.html:
Sub-process IDE.2
Sub-process nameIdentify controls protecting the system to be used.
Sub-process descriptionThis sub-process is used to identify components, system functions, processes, or other measures that are used to ensure that the system operates within acceptable parameters.

Beginning at the subcomponent level, identify all controls that ensure that the program, systems, and components operate within acceptable parameters. Identify system components that monitor or protect critical subcomponents. Then review critical components and identify any system functions that provide those same assurances. Next, identify external systems, programmatic activities, processes, procedures, and practices that serve to monitor or protect the system. Identify any programmatic activities that serve to monitor or protect the program itself.

Using the interactions, intersections, connections, and dependencies identified in E.1, Identify and Map Interactions, Intersections, Connections, and Dependencies across Program, System/Subsystem, and Component/Subcomponent, identify controls that monitor and protect those interactions, intersections, connections, and dependencies.

OutputsListing of controls protecting the system to be used to pass to E.3.

contents.html:
Sub-process IDE.5
Sub-process nameAssign Final Criticality Levels to Systems, Subsystems, Components, and Subcomponents
Sub-process descriptionThis sub-process finalizes Baseline Criticality levels determined in processes C and D.

The critical nature of components and systems may be influenced by the interactions, intersections, connections, and dependencies, connections, controls, frequency of use, and impacts identified in Process E. Review the Baseline Criticality levels defined in C.5 and D.5. Considering the outputs of Process E, refine the rankings. Consider ranking:

Components and subcomponents by their importance in keeping the system from entering adverse operating states or keeping the system operational while in adverse operating states; and
Systems and subsystems by their importance in keeping the program from entering adverse operating states or keeping the program running while in adverse operating states.

Avoid reducing the criticality scores of systems and components without carefully considering legal, regulatory, safety, security, privacy, business, and other constraints and managerial decisions. A concatenated score may be used (e.g. using a scale 1 to 5, a combined score of 1.3.2 may show that a component has a “2” rating in a “3” system in a “1” project).

Note that when components support multiple systems, it can be useful to track the criticality of that component to each project in addition to its finalized criticality level. A scoring system may be defined that uses the information from Process E to refine but not alter the Baseline Criticality levels. For example, Baseline Criticality levels could be given a digit identifier from 1 to 5 while results of the review conducted in Process E could add a digit 0 to 9 to that identifier, to make the final identifier a two-digit ranking from 10 to 59.

Whatever method is used to score the criticality levels, ensure that the method is sufficiently detailed so that a reasonably small number of components are given a high criticality score. The process described in this publication usually will not result in a large number of components being given a high criticality score. If this occurs, it may be assumed that many of these components are either outside the scope or control of the program or do not have highest criticality.

In general, a component is not given a higher criticality level than the highest criticality of the systems it supports. Neither would a system have a higher criticality level than the highest criticality of the processes/workflow paths it supports.

Determine the duration for the final criticality level to be valid. Consider the life cycle of the components, systems, and projects under evaluation.

As part of the risk management process related to the system/components, define means to monitor changes to the system and component criticality levels over the life cycle of the project and over the life cycle of those components and systems.
InputsDetailed Review Results from Sub-Process E, Conduct Detailed Review of Risk and Criticality Analysis.
OutputsFinalized criticality for each analyzed component/subcomponent, system/subsystem, etc.
MethodsDocument Review; Brainstorming; Group Decision Making

contents.html_ja:
サブプロセス IDE.5
サブプロセス名システム、サブシステム、コンポーネント、サブコンポーネントへの最終重要度レベルの割り当て
サブプロセスの説明このサブプロセスは、プロセス C と D で決定したベースライン重要度レベルを確定します。

コンポーネントとシステムの重要な性質は、プロセス E で特定した相互作用、交差、接続、依存関係、管理策、使用頻度、影響によって左右される場合があります。C.5 と D.5 で定義したベースライン重要度レベルをレビューしてください。プロセス E の出力を考慮して、順位を精緻化してください。次のように順位付けすることを検討すべきです。

コンポーネントとサブコンポーネントは、システムが好ましくない運用状態に入るのを防ぐこと、または好ましくない運用状態にあってもシステムの運用を維持することにおける重要性に基づいて順位付けします。
システムとサブシステムは、プログラムが好ましくない運用状態に入るのを防ぐこと、または好ましくない運用状態にあってもプログラムの運用を維持することにおける重要性に基づいて順位付けします。

法的、規制上、安全性、セキュリティ、プライバシー、事業上、その他の制約と経営上の判断を慎重に考慮せずに、システムやコンポーネントの重要度スコアを引き下げることは避けてください。連結スコアを使用してもよいです（たとえば、1 から 5 の尺度を用いる場合、1.3.2 という複合スコアは、あるコンポーネントが「1」のプロジェクトにおける「3」のシステム内で「2」の評価であることを示す場合があります）。

コンポーネントが複数のシステムを支える場合、最終的な重要度レベルに加えて、そのコンポーネントの各プロジェクトに対する重要度を追跡すると有用な場合があることに注意してください。プロセス E の情報を用いて、ベースライン重要度レベルを精緻化するが変更しないスコアリング方式を定義してもよいです。たとえば、ベースライン重要度レベルに 1 から 5 の 1 桁の識別子を与え、プロセス E で実施したレビューの結果によってその識別子に 0 から 9 の 1 桁を加え、最終的な識別子を 10 から 59 の 2 桁の順位とすることができます。

重要度レベルのスコアリングにどのような方法を用いる場合でも、高い重要度スコアが与えられるコンポーネントの数が合理的に少なくなるよう、その方法が十分に詳細であることを確実にしてください。本刊行物で説明するプロセスでは、通常、多数のコンポーネントに高い重要度スコアが与えられることにはなりません。そうなった場合は、それらのコンポーネントの多くがプログラムの適用範囲または制御範囲の外にあるか、最高の重要度ではないと考えられます。

一般に、コンポーネントに与えられる重要度レベルは、それが支えるシステムの最高重要度レベルを上回りません。同様に、システムの重要度レベルも、それが支えるプロセス／ワークフローパスの最高重要度レベルを上回りません。

最終的な重要度レベルが有効である期間を判断してください。評価対象のコンポーネント、システム、プロジェクトのライフサイクルを検討してください。

システム／コンポーネントに関連するリスク管理プロセスの一環として、プロジェクトのライフサイクル、およびコンポーネントとシステムのライフサイクルを通じて、システムとコンポーネントの重要度レベルの変化を監視する手段を定義してください。
入力サブプロセス E「リスクと重要度の分析に関する詳細レビューの実施（Conduct Detailed Review of Risk and Criticality Analysis）」の詳細レビューの結果。
出力分析した各コンポーネント／サブコンポーネント、システム／サブシステムなどの確定した重要度。

contents.html: This appendix does not give detailed information on any given method, but provides a short description and reference where more information can be found on how to perform the method.
contents.html_ja: 本付録は、個々の手法について詳細な情報を示すものではなく、その手法の実施方法についてさらに情報を得られる場所の簡単な説明と参照先を示します。

contents.html: Activity Network Diagram – “an activity network diagram, also known as arrow diagram, pert chart, and critical path method, is used to show activities that are in parallel and/or in series. It will show the most likely times, the most pessimistic times, and the most likely times for the completion of projects.” [25]
contents.html_ja: アクティビティネットワーク図（Activity Network Diagram）– 「アクティビティネットワーク図は、矢線図、PERT 図、クリティカルパス法としても知られ、並行または直列で行われる活動を示すために用いられます。プロジェクトの完了に要する最も可能性の高い時間、最も悲観的な時間、および最も楽観的な時間を示します。」[25]
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p72と照合し一致

contents.html: Architecture Definition – “provides a formal model of the Baseline Architecture, Target Architecture, and the gaps between the two states.” [27]
contents.html_ja: アーキテクチャ定義（Architecture Definition）– 「ベースラインアーキテクチャ、ターゲットアーキテクチャ、およびその 2 つの状態の間のギャップの正式なモデルを提供します。」[27]
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p72と照合し一致

contents.html: Brainstorming or Brainstorming of Activities – “a team activity that seeks to produce a broad or diverse set of options through the rapid and uncritical generation of ideas.” [1]
contents.html_ja: ブレインストーミング、または活動のブレインストーミング（Brainstorming or Brainstorming of Activities）– 「アイデアを迅速かつ批判を挟まずに生み出すことで、幅広く多様な選択肢を生み出そうとするチーム活動。」[1]
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p72と照合し一致

contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p72と照合し一致

contents.html: Document Review – data collection method for the review of documentation received throughout the criticality analysis process(es)/sub-process(es). contents.html_ja: 文書レビュー（Document Review）– 重要度分析のプロセス／サブプロセス全体を通じて受け取る文書をレビューするための、データ収集の方法。イントラネットサイトや文書管理システムのレビュー、あるいは司書やその他の文書管理の専門家の活用を伴う場合があります。[1]

contents.html_ja: 機能分解（Functional Decomposition）– プロセス、機能領域、または成果物を構成部分に分解し、各部分を独立して分析できるようにすること。[1]

contents.html: Gantt Chart – a visual representation of a project schedule. A Gantt chart is a type of bar chart in which a series of horizontal lines shows the amount of work done or production completed in certain periods of time in relation to the amount planned for those periods. [23]
contents.html_ja: ガントチャート（Gantt Chart）– プロジェクトスケジュールの視覚的な表現。ガントチャートは棒グラフの一種で、一連の横線によって、特定の期間に行われた作業量または完了した生産量を、それらの期間に計画された量との関係で示します。[23]
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p72と照合し一致

contents.html: An organization is replacing the asset management portion of their Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system. The new system will process a variety of data including potentially sensitive personnel and mission data. It will connect to other portions of the ERP system, including human resources, acquisition/supply chain, and finance applications. The system will consist of a mixture of custom-built and COTS hardware and software components.

contents.html: The Project Manager reviews the organization’s strategic plan, risk management plan, and other documentation and determines that the organization does not have any formal criticality analysis procedures. The Project Manager does not have the authority nor the time and ability to perform a criticality analysis of the entire organization, which would be ideal. However, it is early enough in the ERP project that an analysis can be written into the project plan prior to and concordant with system procurement and implementation.
contents.html_ja: プロジェクトマネージャーは、組織の戦略計画、リスク管理計画、その他の文書をレビューし、組織に正式な重要度分析手順がないと判断します。プロジェクトマネージャーには、理想的ではあるものの組織全体の重要度分析を行う権限も時間も能力もありません。しかし、ERP プロジェクトはまだ十分早い段階にあるため、システムの調達および実装に先立ち、それらと歩調を合わせて分析を行うことをプロジェクト計画に盛り込めます。

contents.html: A.1 The Project Manager delegates to an employee with business analysis training, the process of integrating criticality analysis activities into the project plan. The Business Analyst<sup>9</sup> uses the Criticality Analysis Process Model in this publication to determine appropriate tasks, roles, and responsibilities based on Processes B, C, D, and E of the Model. The Project Manager and Business Analyst coordinate with a legal representative to identify laws, regulations, and organizational policies which may impact the project; they discuss with the rest of the project team how the criticality analysis may align with or impact their normal activities and discuss ways to address any concerns they have. The Business Analyst works with the project team to compare the guidance in the Related Processes Outside of Criticality Analysis in each Process and Sub-process description with the organization’s existing processes to ensure that security engineering and risk management processes are appropriately integrated and planned for.

contents.html: Once the project begins, the Project Manager ensures that procedures for conducting a criticality analysis have been adequately defined and are appropriate to be used for this system integration effort. They then decide on the thresholds grouping the components into High, Moderate, and Low groups, which become the Baseline Criticality levels for each component.
contents.html_ja: システムエンジニアは、ソフトウェアアプリケーションのコンポーネント（ユーザーの挙動などの非ソフトウェアのコンポーネントを含む）を、最も重要なものから最も重要でないものへと順位付けします。彼らは、この情報を用いて、開発プロセスでどの機能を優先し、どの機能を後回しにしてもよいかを決定します。続いて、コンポーネントを高、中、低のグループにグループ化するためのしきい値を決定します。これが各コンポーネントのベースライン重要度レベルになります。

contents.html: D.1-5 (multiple iterations) Because the development of the software application is following an agile methodology, they repeat the criticality analysis in parallel with the development of the application. D.1 and D.2 are used to help scope the tasks and identify the functions which will be developed or improved and are conducted during sprint planning meetings; D.3 is completed during the sprint as part of documentation; D.4 and D.5 are done during the testing and evaluation portions of the sprint. In a few cases, the systems engineers decided to do an additional, more detailed iteration of the analysis to identify critical subcomponents of highly critical components. This was done, for example, with the user interface, and helped identify user inputs that might exploit a vulnerability resulting in an impact to the integrity or availability of the database.
contents.html_ja: D.1-5（複数回の反復）ソフトウェアアプリケーションの開発はアジャイル手法に従っているため、彼らはアプリケーションの開発と並行して重要度分析を繰り返します。D.1 と D.2 は、タスクのスコープを設定し、開発または改善される機能を特定するのに役立てるために用いられ、スプリント計画会議で実施されます。D.3 は、文書化の一環としてスプリント中に完了します。D.4 と D.5 は、スプリントのテストと評価の部分で行われます。いくつかのケースでは、システムエンジニアは、重要度が高いコンポーネントの重要なサブコンポーネントを特定するために、さらに詳細な分析の反復を追加で行うことにしました。これはたとえばユーザーインタフェースについて行われ、データベースの完全性または可用性に影響を及ぼす脆弱性を悪用しうるユーザー入力の特定に役立ちました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p83と照合し一致

contents.html: Process E
contents.html_ja: プロセス E
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本の例Aの小見出し（太字斜体、Action の下）

contents.html: With Baseline Criticalities assigned across the program activities/workflow paths, subsystems of the system under development, and components/subcomponents, the Project Manager, Lead Systems Architect, Lead Systems Engineer, and lead security engineer and privacy engineer begin to review baseline criticalities for consistency, interdependencies, and to develop final subsystem and component/subcomponent criticality levels. They also include the ERP program manager in this analysis as the system is closely connected to and tied with others under the ERP system umbrella.
contents.html_ja: プログラムの活動／ワークフローパス、開発中のシステムのサブシステム、コンポーネント／サブコンポーネントのすべてにベースライン重要度が割り当てられると、プロジェクトマネージャー、主任システムアーキテクト、主任システムエンジニア、主任セキュリティエンジニア、主任プライバシーエンジニアは、整合性と相互依存性についてベースライン重要度のレビューを開始し、サブシステムおよびコンポーネント／サブコンポーネントの最終的な重要度レベルを作成します。システムは ERP システムの傘下にある他のシステムと密接に接続され結び付いているため、彼らはこの分析に ERP プログラムマネージャーも加えます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p83と照合し一致

contents.html: E.1 Those persons responsible for conducting processes B, C, and D, meet to review the artifacts and results from their respective processes. They identify connection points where data or information will flow between components, any components across the different subsystems which are very similar in functionality, which components or component types will be used to support more than one subsystem, groups of components supplied by the same manufacturer, and finally groups of components expected to fail around the same time frame. The group performs this same analysis for the subsystems, identifying connections, commonalities, and repetitions. The tracing of components all the way through the program activities and workflows helps to identify any interdependencies that have not been considered in the analysis up to this point. The group documents result of this analysis using diagrams of interdependencies. They determine that there was a set of interdependencies and duplications across the inventory management system and the broader ERP system related to modifying inventory information.
contents.html_ja: E.1 プロセス B、C、D の実施に責任を負う者が集まり、それぞれのプロセスの成果物と結果をレビューします。彼らは、コンポーネント間でデータや情報が流れる接続点、異なるサブシステムにまたがって機能が非常によく似ているコンポーネント、複数のサブシステムを支えるために使われるコンポーネントまたはコンポーネントの種類、同じ製造者が供給するコンポーネントのグループ、そしてほぼ同じ時期に故障すると予想されるコンポーネントのグループを特定します。グループは、同じ分析をサブシステムについても行い、接続、共通点、繰り返しを特定します。コンポーネントをプログラムの活動とワークフローを通じて最後までたどることで、ここまでの分析では考慮されていなかった相互依存関係の特定に役立ちます。グループは、この分析の結果を相互依存関係の図を用いて文書化します。この分析の結果、在庫情報の変更に関連する一連の相互依存関係と重複が、在庫管理システムとより広範な ERP システムとの間にあると判断しました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p83と照合し一致

contents.html: E.2 The group then identifies what existing controls have been designated to monitor and protect the system, subsystems, and components. These controls include traditional security controls such as access control, configuration management, secure design principles, network and system activity monitoring functions, software switches, etc., as well as privacy controls such as notices, de-identification measures, privacy-enhancing cryptographic protocols, data tags, privacy-protective sensor configurations, etc.; they may be automated, technical, or manual. These controls can be documented in a variety of places, including security and privacy requirements, security and privacy plans, risk treatment plans, etc. The group determines that some controls included in the design may be excessive and that no control existed to prevent a resource shortage with regards to the interdependencies identified in E.1. The engineers responsible for those components modify their design slightly to compensate and the group reanalyzes the impact of the operating states of the components and controls.
contents.html_ja: E.2 続いてグループは、システム、サブシステム、コンポーネントを監視し保護するために、どのような既存の管理策が指定されているかを特定します。これらの管理策には、アクセス制御、構成管理、セキュア設計原則、ネットワークおよびシステムの活動の監視機能、ソフトウェアスイッチなどの従来のセキュリティ管理策に加え、通知、非識別化の対策、プライバシー強化暗号プロトコル、データタグ、プライバシーを保護するセンサー構成などのプライバシー管理策が含まれます。これらは、自動化されたもの、技術的なもの、手作業のもののいずれでもかまいません。これらの管理策は、セキュリティ・プライバシー要件、セキュリティ・プライバシー計画、リスク対応計画など、さまざまな場所に文書化できます。グループは、設計に含まれる管理策の一部が過剰である可能性があり、E.1 で特定した相互依存関係に関してリソース不足を防ぐ管理策が存在しなかったと判断します。それらのコンポーネントに責任を負うエンジニアは、補うために設計を少し修正し、グループはコンポーネントと管理策の運用状態の影響を再分析します。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p84と照合し一致

contents.html: E.3 The group then traces the impact of operating states that were defined in B.4, C.4, and D.4 to determine what adverse operating states may have a cascading effect across the subsystems, system, and project processes. The group reviews the controls in place at each level and what would happen to the program if the control(s) entered an adverse operating state. The group finds that a failure in one portion of the software application could lead to a cascading failure of the broader ERP system.
contents.html_ja: E.3 続いてグループは、B.4、C.4、D.4 で定義した運用状態の影響をたどり、サブシステム、システム、プロジェクトのプロセスにまたがって連鎖的な影響を及ぼしうる、悪影響を及ぼす運用状態を判断します。グループは、各レベルで導入されている管理策と、その管理策が悪影響を及ぼす運用状態に入った場合にプログラムに何が起こるかをレビューします。グループは、ソフトウェアアプリケーションの一部の障害が、より広範な ERP システムの連鎖的な障害につながりうることを見いだします。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p84と照合し一致

contents.html: E.4 Next, the group reviews available security and privacy risk documentation to see if components/subcomponents, the subsystems, or the system itself should be assigned a higher criticality level than what has been assigned during the process thus far. Using existing risk assessment, threat assessment, impact analysis, or any similar documentation, the group evaluates the controls identified in E.2, the impact of operating states on those controls in E.3, and the Baseline Criticality Levels assigned in processes B, C, and D. It was determined that some of the components originally designated as lower criticality were connected to portions of the ERP system which, if an incorrect input was provided, would have significant impact. The criticality levels of these components were increased. The criticality levels of controls which may protect against such an event were also increased.
contents.html_ja: E.4 次に、グループは、利用可能なセキュリティとプライバシーのリスク文書をレビューし、コンポーネント／サブコンポーネント、サブシステム、またはシステム自体に、これまでのプロセスで割り当てたものより高い重要度レベルを割り当てるべきかどうかを確認します。既存のリスクアセスメント、脅威アセスメント、影響分析、または同様の文書を用いて、グループは、E.2 で特定した管理策、E.3 でそれらの管理策に対する運用状態の影響、プロセス B、C、D で割り当てたベースライン重要度レベルを評価します。当初は重要度が低いと指定されていたコンポーネントの一部が、ERP システムの、誤った入力が与えられると重大な影響が生じる部分に接続されていると判断されました。これらのコンポーネントの重要度レベルは引き上げられました。そのような事象から保護しうる管理策の重要度レベルも引き上げられました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p84と照合し一致

contents.html: E.5 Finally, the group reviews analysis results from Process E to determine how Baseline Criticality Levels that were assigned to the system, its subsystems, and components/subcomponents should be revised to assign final Criticality Levels. This analysis considers identified interdependencies, controls, and any aspects of the system, subsystem, and component/subcomponent operations that may be vulnerable due to systems architecture and design, reliance on a single supplier, or any other factors that were discovered in the overall analysis.
contents.html_ja: E.5 最後に、グループは、プロセス E の分析結果をレビューして、システム、そのサブシステム、コンポーネント／サブコンポーネントに割り当てたベースライン重要度レベルを、最終的な重要度レベルを割り当てるためにどのように修正すべきかを判断します。この分析では、特定した相互依存関係、管理策、およびシステムアーキテクチャと設計、単一の供給者への依存、または全体の分析で発見されたその他の要因のために脆弱である可能性のある、システム、サブシステム、コンポーネント／サブコンポーネントの運用のあらゆる側面を考慮します。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p84と照合し一致

contents.html: Once Criticality Levels have been finalized, the program manager distributes the results to the groups performing risk analysis, threat analysis, impact analysis, contingency planning, and systems engineering activities. Criticality Levels are then used to inform these activities and help refine how they are planned and performed in the future. Criticality Levels also provide valuable inputs into the design and refinement of security requirements and controls, help shape system and component (hardware and software) testing, determine if any components should be bought in advance and stockpiled, and to inform supplier diversification decisions.
contents.html_ja: 重要度レベルが確定すると、プログラムマネージャーは、リスク分析、脅威分析、影響分析、コンティンジェンシープランニング、システムエンジニアリング活動を行うグループに結果を配布します。その後、重要度レベルはこれらの活動に情報を提供し、今後それらをどのように計画し実施するかを洗練するのに役立ちます。重要度レベルはまた、セキュリティ要件と管理策の設計と洗練への貴重な入力となり、システムとコンポーネント（ハードウェアとソフトウェア）のテストを形作り、いずれかのコンポーネントを事前に購入して備蓄すべきかどうかを判断し、供給者の多様化に関する判断にも役立ちます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p84と照合し一致

contents.html: Later, Criticality Levels are used to inform future system development and integration efforts, as well as future procurements and modernization efforts.
contents.html_ja: その後、重要度レベルは、将来のシステム開発と統合の取り組み、および将来の調達と近代化の取り組みに情報を提供するために使われます。

contents.html: D.2 Example B – SmartCity Concept Development
contents.html_ja: D.2 例 B – SmartCity のコンセプト開発
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p86の節見出し

contents.html: An organization is considering developing a plot of land encompassing about 200 acres. The CEO of the organization would like to use the land to create a futuristic “smart city” (called “Smartstown, USA”). Because there is a lot of talk about privacy and cybersecurity, the CEO wants Smartstown, USA, to be safe, secure, and attractive to both businesses and residents. The organization is concerned that such a goal is unreasonable, and that this large and innovative project has a high likelihood of failure. They have spoken with many subject matter experts, both inside and outside of the organization, and found that there is little consensus regarding an approach to take; each expert views their area of expertise as being critical to the success of the project and experts are unwilling to compromise. The organization decides to conduct a high-level criticality analysis to identify key areas of risk, which they can then focus on in more depth.

They decide that they will be performing at least two system-level analyses: one for the transportation infrastructure, and one for the medical/dental infrastructure. This example will focus on the transportation infrastructure.
contents.html_ja: プロセス C から得た情報を用いて、組織はシステムレベルの分析を実施します。彼らは、少なくとも 2 つのシステムレベルの分析を実施することにします。1 つは交通インフラ、もう 1 つは医療／歯科インフラです。この例では、交通インフラに焦点を当てます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p88と照合し一致

contents.html: C-1 The organization develops working groups for each analysis. The transportation working group is composed of urban planners, legal representatives, transportation experts, automotive vehicle researchers, and others. Each workshop agrees to a set of rules. They set a time limit of ½ day for their analyses. Prior to the workshop, the participants are given information from Process B to review.
contents.html_ja: C-1 組織は、各分析のためにワーキンググループを設けます。交通のワーキンググループは、都市計画者、法務担当者、交通の専門家、自動車研究者などで構成されます。各ワークショップでは、参加者が一連のルールに合意します。分析に割り当てる時間は半日とします。ワークショップに先立ち、参加者にはプロセス B の情報が渡され、参加者はそれをレビューします。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p89と照合し一致

contents.html: C-2 The working group reviews the scenarios developed in Process B. They brainstorm a list of every transportation-related function and capability needed to support those scenarios. To help with this process, they ask the questions “Who uses the infrastructure?” and “How is it used?” They use both the information from Process B as well as their own expert knowledge to answer this question.
contents.html_ja: C-2 ワーキンググループは、プロセス B で作成したシナリオをレビューします。彼らは、それらのシナリオを支えるために必要な、交通に関連するすべての機能と能力をブレインストーミングして一覧にします。このプロセスを助けるために、彼らは「誰がそのインフラを使うか」「どのように使われるか」という質問をします。彼らは、この質問に答えるために、プロセス B の情報と自らの専門知識の両方を使います。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p89と照合し一致

contents.html: They decide that the roads should allow for smooth flow of traffic allowing residents a predictable travel time. There must be infrastructure in place to support newer vehicle types such as electric, hybrid, and autonomous vehicles. The group decides to plan for the increased use of delivery services and to ensure that delivery vehicles do not obstruct traffic. Public transportation is heavily used in the nearby metropolitan area, and so the group decides to support commuters who wish to travel to the metropolitan area by providing connecting public transportation services. During this brainstorming exercise, the group roughly prioritizes the functions and criticalities listed.
contents.html_ja: 彼らは、道路は、住民が予測可能な移動時間を得られるよう、円滑な交通の流れを可能にすべきだと判断します。電気自動車、ハイブリッド車、自動運転車などの新しい車種を支えるインフラが整っていなければなりません。グループは、配送サービスの利用の増加に備えて計画し、配送車両が交通を妨げないようにすることを決めます。近隣の大都市圏では公共交通機関が多く使われているため、グループは、接続する公共交通サービスを提供することで、大都市圏へ移動したい通勤者を支援することにします。このブレインストーミングの演習の間に、グループは、一覧にした機能と重要度に大まかに優先順位を付けます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p89と照合し一致

contents.html: C-3 The group begins identifying what types of systems might be used to support the functions and requirements defined in C-2. This process often results in the identification of additional requirements and functions. They list things such as roads, crosswalks/bridges, gas stations, electric vehicle charging stations, signage and painting that support automated vehicles, the vehicles themselves, and the communications systems that allow vehicles to communicate with other systems (e.g., GPS). They also identify the means to clean the streets and drains to ensure that the signage and painting remain visible, accessible transportation stations, reliable and fast train or similar system, reliable bus or tram system, school bus or other transport, support for taxi or other service, parking (public, delivery, bus, repair, long-term, etc.), bicycle and pedestrian paths/lanes, etc. They identify some technologies that are futuristic and bring in experts to identify what sort of things those technologies will need to operate to expand their list.
contents.html_ja: C-3 グループは、C-2 で定義した機能と要件を支えるために、どのような種類のシステムが使われうるかを特定し始めます。このプロセスは、追加の要件と機能の特定につながることがよくあります。彼らは、道路、横断歩道／橋、ガソリンスタンド、電気自動車の充電ステーション、自動運転車を支える標識と路面表示、車両そのもの、車両が他のシステム（たとえば GPS）と通信できるようにする通信システムなどを一覧にします。また、標識と路面表示が見え続けるようにするための道路と排水溝の清掃手段、利用しやすい交通の拠点、信頼性が高く高速な鉄道または同様のシステム、信頼性の高いバスまたは路面電車のシステム、スクールバスやその他の輸送、タクシーやその他のサービスの支援、駐車場（公共、配送、バス、修理、長期など）、自転車と歩行者の道／レーンなども特定します。彼らは、未来的な技術をいくつか特定し、それらの技術の運用に何が必要かを特定して一覧を拡張するために、専門家を招きます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p89と照合し一致

contents.html: C-4 The group loosely defines a set of rules for each function/requirement by which one could tell that the system is operating at peak efficiency. For example, the drive time between point X and point Y will be 30 to 35 minutes. The group then loosely defines adverse operating states for each function and requirement defined. They also roughly assign significance levels for the operating states. For example, in the case GPS functionality:
contents.html_ja: C-4 グループは、各機能／要件について、システムが最高の効率で運用されていると判断できる一連のルールを緩やかに定義します。たとえば、地点 X と地点 Y の間の運転時間は 30 分から 35 分です。続いてグループは、定義した各機能と要件について、悪影響を及ぼす運用状態を緩やかに定義します。また、運用状態に重要度の水準を大まかに割り当てます。たとえば、GPS の機能の場合は次のとおりです。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p89と照合し一致

contents.html: (1-Low) If GPS does not work in the area, drivers may be unable to reach their destinations and may create congestion as they drive around trying to find places.
contents.html_ja: (1-低) その地域で GPS が機能しない場合、運転者が目的地に到達できず、場所を探して走り回ることで渋滞を引き起こす可能性があります。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p89と照合し一致

contents.html: (2-Low-Moderate) If GPS works sporadically or slowly in the area, it may distract or cause drivers to miss a turn, which may cause them to swerve and potentially cause an accident.
contents.html_ja: (2-低から中) その地域で GPS の動作が断続的または遅い場合、GPS によって運転者の注意がそらされたり、曲がり角を見逃したりすることがあり、その結果、急ハンドルを切って事故を引き起こす可能性があります。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p89と照合し一致

contents.html: (3-Moderate-High) If GPS in the area is compromised, it could result in the theft of personally identifiable information (PII) and potentially the modification of GPS data, and aggregation of travel points could permit the tracking of persons (including high-profile persons and children) and could reveal sensitive information, including health information, religious activity, and other personal habits.
contents.html_ja: (3-中から高) その地域の GPS が危殆化した場合、個人を特定できる情報（PII）の窃取や、GPS データの改ざんにつながる可能性があり、移動地点の集約によって（著名人や子どもを含む）人物の追跡が可能になり、健康情報、宗教的活動、その他の個人の習慣を含む機微な情報が明らかになる可能性があります。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p89と照合し一致

contents.html: (4-Low) GPS operating more efficiently than needed would waste resources.
contents.html_ja: (4-低) GPS が必要以上に効率的に運用されると、資源が無駄になります。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p90と照合し一致

contents.html: (5-Low) If GPS in the area has extraneous information, it could cause confusion.
contents.html_ja: (5-低) その地域の GPS に余分な情報が含まれていると、混乱を招く可能性があります。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p90と照合し一致

contents.html: C-5 The group reviews the operation states of each function/requirement and ranks them in terms of impact. The group finds that communications between vehicles and the transportation infrastructure is by far the most impactful element, whether it is the drivers reading road signs or autonomous vehicles registering an approaching emergency vehicle.
contents.html_ja: C-5 グループは、各機能／要件の運用状態をレビューし、影響の観点から順位付けします。グループは、運転者が道路標識を読む場合でも、自動運転車が接近する緊急車両を認識する場合でも、車両と交通インフラの間の通信が、圧倒的に影響の大きい要素であることを見いだします。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p90と照合し一致

contents.html: Process D
contents.html_ja: プロセス D
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本の例Bの小見出し（太字斜体）

contents.html: The organization decides to narrow the analysis further to identify critical components of the system. They tailor this analysis to their organization and to the scope of the analysis. They perform step D-4 prior to step D-3 (for this example, the steps are numbered as in the model, but are rearranged). A group is formed consisting of experts in the fields of transportation, including urban planners, automated vehicle researchers, network and vehicle designers/engineers, and cybersecurity and privacy professionals.
contents.html_ja: 組織は、システムの重要なコンポーネントを特定するために、分析をさらに絞り込むことにします。彼らは、この分析を自らの組織と分析のスコープに合わせて調整します。彼らはステップ D-4 をステップ D-3 の前に実施します（この例では、ステップの番号はモデルのとおりですが、順序は入れ替えています）。都市計画者、自動運転車の研究者、ネットワークと車両の設計者／エンジニア、サイバーセキュリティとプライバシーの専門家を含む、交通分野の専門家で構成されるグループが編成されます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p90と照合し一致

contents.html: D-1 Because the analysis is limited in scope to theoretical applications without identifying any specific technology solutions, the working group cannot conduct a thorough analysis of risks in this area. Non-electronic communication was determined to be out of scope for this analysis. They decide to have a one-day workshop to collect what they can from a high-level perspective.
contents.html_ja: D-1 分析のスコープが、特定の技術ソリューションを特定しない理論上の応用に限定されているため、ワーキンググループは、この分野のリスクについて徹底的な分析を行うことができません。電子的でない通信は、この分析のスコープ外と判断されました。彼らは、高レベルの観点から集められるものを集めるために、1 日のワークショップを行うことにします。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p90と照合し一致

contents.html: D-2 The group begins by identifying all the components that are involved in the concept of communicating between a vehicle and the infrastructure. They list things such as: the car itself; the driver; the sensors in a car used to aid the driver; the mechanisms in an automated vehicle used to process data from sensors; the mechanisms in an automated vehicle to translate that data into commands which the car will follow; and the electronic communication between the vehicle and the infrastructure. (e.g., GPS communications or if a stop light notifies cars in the area that it is turning red. Non-electronic communication is out of scope for this example.)
contents.html_ja: D-2 グループは、車両とインフラの間の通信という概念に関わるすべてのコンポーネントを特定することから始めます。彼らは、車自体、運転者、運転者を支援するために車に搭載されたセンサー、自動運転車でセンサーからのデータを処理する仕組み、自動運転車でそのデータを、車が従うコマンドに変換する仕組み、車両とインフラの間の電子的な通信などを一覧にします。（たとえば、GPS 通信や、信号機が赤に変わることを周辺の車に通知する場合など。電子的でない通信は、この例ではスコープ外です。）
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p90と照合し一致

contents.html: The group reviews the components listed and identifies how each of them are connected. In some cases, additional components are included. The group finds that there are several workflow paths depending on the communication origin, but that all the workflow paths use the same set of processes to register and interpret the communication.
contents.html_ja: グループは、一覧にしたコンポーネントをレビューし、それぞれがどのように接続されているかを特定します。場合によっては、追加のコンポーネントが含まれます。グループは、通信の発信元によっていくつかのワークフローパスがあるものの、すべてのワークフローパスが、通信を認識し解釈するために同じ一連のプロセスを使っていることを見いだします。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p90と照合し一致

contents.html: D-4 The group defines operating states for each component type. For example, for a sensor:
contents.html_ja: D-4 グループは、各コンポーネントの種類について運用状態を定義します。たとえば、センサーの場合は次のとおりです。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p90と照合し一致

contents.html: (1-Moderate-High) If a sensor does not function, the vehicle will not register a warning such as an approaching obstacle and may cause an accident.
contents.html_ja: (1-中から高) センサーが機能しない場合、車両は接近する障害物などの警告を認識できず、その結果、事故が起こる可能性があります。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p90と照合し一致

contents.html: (2-Moderate-High) If a sensor is slow, it may have the same results as if it didn’t operate at all.
contents.html_ja: (2-中から高) センサーが遅い場合、まったく動作しない場合と同じ結果になる可能性があります。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p90と照合し一致

contents.html: (3-High) If a sensor operates erratically or is compromised, it may register an obstacle when there isn’t one and cause an accident.
contents.html_ja: (3-高) センサーが不安定に動作する、または危殆化した場合、障害物がないのにあると認識し、事故を引き起こす可能性があります。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p91と照合し一致

contents.html: (4-Moderate) If a sensor operates overly efficiently, potentially collecting additional information or information in greater detail than was anticipated, privacy problems may arise.
contents.html_ja: (4-中) センサーが過度に効率的に動作し、想定を超える追加の情報や、より詳細な情報を収集する可能性がある場合、プライバシーの問題が生じる可能性があります。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p91と照合し一致

contents.html: (5-High) If a sensor operates as expected, but has an added feature which allows a malicious entity to view the information the sensor collects, it could represent a significant privacy concern.
contents.html_ja: (5-高) センサーが想定どおりに動作するものの、悪意ある主体がセンサーの収集した情報を閲覧できるようにする追加機能を備えている場合、重大なプライバシー上の懸念になりえます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p91と照合し一致

contents.html: D-3 The group decides that, because of the scope of this analysis, they cannot reasonably identify the individual components which will be used. Instead, they list the types of components used, such as “sensor,” “interpreter,” “analyzer,” and “operator.” They create a system diagram showing the workflow paths as they move through each process and component type.
contents.html_ja: D-3 グループは、この分析のスコープのため、使用される個々のコンポーネントを合理的に特定することはできないと判断します。代わりに、使用されるコンポーネントの種類を、「センサー」「インタプリタ」「アナライザ」「オペレータ」のように一覧にします。彼らは、各プロセスとコンポーネントの種類を経由するワークフローパスを示すシステム図を作成します。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p91と照合し一致

contents.html: D-5 The group collects all the various operating states and scenarios to develop baseline criticality levels for the components. They decide that the sensors and the operator component types are the most critical as they had the most significant impact in this scope.
contents.html_ja: D-5 グループは、さまざまな運用状態とシナリオをすべて集めて、コンポーネントのベースライン重要度レベルを作成します。彼らは、このスコープで最も大きな影響があったことから、センサーとオペレータのコンポーネントの種類が最も重要であると判断します。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p91と照合し一致

contents.html: Process E
contents.html_ja: プロセス E
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本の例Bの小見出し（太字斜体）

contents.html: The organization collects all the information that was created in each of the component-level analyses. They find that, overall, there were five different components that were considered “critical.” They chose to continue the analysis with these five components. Again, for this analysis, they chose to tailor the analysis to their needs.
contents.html_ja: 組織は、各コンポーネントレベルの分析で作成されたすべての情報を集めます。全体として、「重要」とみなされたコンポーネントが 5 つあったことがわかります。彼らは、この 5 つのコンポーネントで分析を続けることにしました。ここでも、この分析では、分析を自らのニーズに合わせて調整することにしました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p91と照合し一致

contents.html: E-1 The organization assigns representatives from each component-level analysis to meet with representatives from the system-level analysis. They will in turn meet with representatives from the process-level analysis. They set a time limit for this portion of the analysis.
contents.html_ja: E-1 組織は、各コンポーネントレベルの分析の代表者を割り当て、システムレベルの分析の代表者と会合させます。続いて、これらの代表者はプロセスレベルの分析の代表者と会合します。組織は、分析のこの部分に時間制限を設けます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p91と照合し一致

contents.html: E-2 The component-level teams review their analysis with the system-level and process-level representatives. For the communication component group, they review how sensors connect to and interact with other components in the system, and then other components of the smartcity, including those identified by the Medical/Dental working group (the other process besides transportation that was identified as highly critical). They find that sensors play a major role in the transportation system beyond the scope of their analysis. For example, sensors detecting congestion may activate a traffic response such as opening an additional lane, increasing tolls, or rerouting vehicles. The group brainstorms various controls at each level which may help prevent, detect, or respond to a problem. They review what might happen if the control fails and the likelihood of that happening.
contents.html_ja: E-2 コンポーネントレベルのチームは、システムレベルおよびプロセスレベルの代表者と分析をレビューします。通信コンポーネント群は、センサーがシステム内の他のコンポーネントとどのように接続し、相互作用するかをレビューし、さらに、医療／歯科のワーキンググループ（交通以外で重要度が高いと特定されたもう1つのプロセス）が特定したものを含む、スマートシティの他のコンポーネントもレビューします。彼らは、センサーが分析のスコープを超えて交通システムで大きな役割を果たしていることを見いだします。たとえば、渋滞を検知するセンサーは、追加車線の開放、通行料の引き上げ、車両の迂回といった交通対応を作動させる場合があります。グループは、問題の防止、検知、または対応に役立つ可能性のある各レベルのさまざまな管理策をブレインストーミングします。管理策が機能しなかった場合に何が起こりうるか、また、それが起こる可能性をレビューします。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p91と照合し一致

contents.html: E-3 The component-level teams review their operating states and scenarios with the rest of the group. They review how the controls identified in E-2 reduce the likelihood of the impact. In certain cases, they identify areas where they feel the baseline criticality levels don’t represent the levels of impact or likelihood. For example, when comparing all the critical components, they find that the sensors which were identified as critical in the transportation process were also found to be critical in the medical/dental process because the emergency response vehicles are expected to communicate with the traffic signals and with automated vehicles to allow them safe and speedy passage. In addition, they use GPS and other communication technologies. It was found that most every process used a significant amount of wireless communication, and this might place a strain on the communications network.

Executive Summary

The Information Technology Laboratory (ITL) at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) promotes the U.S. economy and public welfare by providing technical leadership for the Nation’s measurement and standards infrastructure. ITL develops tests, test methods, reference data, proof of concept implementations, and technical analyses to advance the development and productive use of information technology. ITL’s responsibilities include the development of management, administrative, technical, and physical standards and guidelines for the cost-effective security and privacy of other than national security-related information in federal information systems.

In the modern world, where complex systems and systems-of-systems are integral to the functioning of society and businesses, it is increasingly important to be able to understand and manage risks that these systems and components may present to the missions that they support. However, in the world of finite resources, it is not possible to apply equal protection to all assets. This publication describes a comprehensive Criticality Analysis Process Model – a structured method of prioritizing programs, systems, and components based on their importance to the goals of an organization and the impact that their inadequate operation or loss may present to those goals. A criticality analysis can help organizations identify and better understand the systems, subsystems, components, and subcomponents that are most essential to their operations and the environment in which they operate. That understanding facilitates better decision making related to the management of an organization’s information assets, including information security and privacy risk management, project management, acquisition, maintenance, and upgrade decisions. The Model is structured to logically follow how organizations design and implement projects and systems, can be used as a component of a holistic and comprehensive risk management approach that considers all risks, and can be used with a variety of risk management standards and guidelines.

The authors, Jon Boyens, National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Celia Paulsen (NIST), Nadya Bartol (Boston Consulting Group), and Kristina Winkler (Boston Consulting Group) would like to acknowledge and thank a number of individuals who provided valuable insights and helped to improve this publication. We would especially like to thank Kelley Dempsey (NIST), Victoria Pillitteri (NIST), Dr. Ron Ross (NIST), Maureen Moore (NIST), Paul Black (NIST), Elizabeth Lennon (NIST), Dr. Carol Woody (SEI CERT), and John Peterson (Redhorse Corporation) for their contribution to the content during the document development and review.

This document is meant to help its users prioritize critical programs, systems, and components. It is not meant as a stand-alone process, rather it is meant to integrate into already existing processes, such as risk management, information security, security engineering, system and software engineering, privacy engineering, safety, quality, and other related disciplines. The model as described represents an idealized process and may not match every organization’s existing processes; readers are encouraged to adapt and integrate the process model described in this publication in a way that best fits the needs and current operations of their organization(s).

A. Define Criticality Analysis Procedure(s) where the organization develops or adopts a set of procedures for performing a criticality analysis. B. Conduct Program-Level Criticality Analysis where the program manager defines, reviews, and analyzes the program to identify key activities that are vital to reaching the objectives of the program and for reaching the overall goals of the organization. C. Conduct System/Subsystem-Level Criticality Analysis where the system designer reviews and analyzes the system or subsystem from the point of view of its criticality to the overall organizational goals. D. Conduct Component/Subcomponent-Level Criticality Analysis where the system or component engineer reviews and analyzes component or subcomponent from the point of view of its criticality to a specific system or subsystem of which these components and subcomponents are a part. E. Conduct Detailed Review of Criticality for Processes B, C, and D where the program manager or a collaborative group analyzes baseline criticality analysis results to create final criticality levels for Systems/Subsystems and Components/Subcomponents.

NISTIR 8179 describes a Criticality Analysis Process Model – a structured method of prioritizing programs, systems, and components based on their importance to the mission and the risk that their ineffective or unsatisfactory operation or loss may present to the mission. The Criticality Analysis Process Model presented in this document adopts and adapts concepts presented in risk management, system engineering, software engineering, security engineering, privacy engineering, safety applications, business analysis, systems analysis, acquisition guidance, and cyber supply chain risk management publications.

The Criticality Analysis Process Model can be used as a component of a holistic and comprehensive risk management approach that considers all risks, including information security and privacy risks. The Model can be used with a variety of risk management standards and guidelines including the International Organization for Standardization/International Electrotechnical Commission (ISO/IEC) 27000 family of standards and the suite of National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Special Publications (SPs). The Model can also be used with systems and software engineering frameworks.

The need for criticality analysis within information security emerged as systems have become more complex and supply chains used to create software, hardware, and services have become extended, geographically distributed, and vast. The first mention of criticality analysis in NIST publications is in NIST SP 800-53 Revision 4 (Rev 4), Security and Privacy Controls for Federal Information Systems and Organizations. Today, criticality analysis is referenced in several NIST special publications including those addressing risk management, system security engineering, and supply chain risk management.

The Model references and uses the outputs and artifacts of risk management, information security, project management, system design, safety, privacy, and other activities that an organization may already be performing. To reduce potential redundancy and duplication, the Model identifies integration points with these existing processes.
The Criticality Analysis Process Model is structured to logically follow how organizations design and implement projects and systems and can be adapted to fit organizations’ unique practices.
The Model consists of five main processes:

Using this Criticality Analysis Process Model can help organizations to better understand the systems, subsystems, components, and subcomponents that are most essential to their operations. Having this information will facilitate holistic information security and privacy risk management and integration of security and privacy considerations into project management and acquisition. The Model can help increase robustness and granularity of the decisions made about levels of protection afforded to systems and components during system development and acquisition life cycles. It also provides a means for communicating and coordinating priorities with product and service providers.

original_blocks.html:
defines the scope, describes any assumptions to be made, identifies responsible parties, and details the procedures to be used in conducting the analysis. It may be tailored to, for example, existing procedures which supersede or align closely with procedures in the model, define how specific sub-processes are to be completed, or rearrange the sub-processes to better fit organizational processes. Because the criticality analysis will likely be performed by multiple groups and individuals, ensure that the proceedure definition includes requirements as to how the groups and individuals are to communicate. Include requirements for any documents that may be transferred between individuals; ensure those individuals have appropriate permissions to review the information in those documents. Include in the procedure what events or conditions (i.e., triggers) result in the need for a criticality analysis. Some organizations may also define the events or conditions (i.e., triggers) that will launch each stage(s) of the analysis. Describe what events or conditions (i.e., triggers) necessitate a full or partial review/update of existing criticality analysis, and how those events or conditions will be monitored for and reported. For example, a review/update may be needed if a new vulnerability is discovered, the environment of operation changes, or a modification to a portion of the system is proposed. original_blocks.html: Sub-process ID B.1 Sub-process name Define or Obtain Program-Level Needs, Goals, Objectives, Assumptions and Constraints Sub-process This process helps define the program being analyzed. It lays the foundation description for the criticality analysis, establishes context, and provides a common perspective on the assumptions, constraints, risk tolerances, and priorities/trade-offs used for making investment and operational decisions. Define how the success or failure of the program will be measured. Identify a high-level objective or set of related objectives. It is best if there is only one objective or if the set of objectives are closely related to focus the analysis. Measurable goals for the objective(s) are described and include any high-level organizational goals that apply. Consider security, safety, privacy, and other related goals. If there are several objectives and goals, consider their priorities and documenting these priorities. Requirements or constraints are clearly identified and may include applicable legal regulations, organizational policy, risk tolerance, budgets, and any other constraints that may impact the flexibility of the organization’s activities. Finally, any assumptions that may impact the analysis are defined. These may include environmental, legal, budgetary, or other variables that may have some degree of uncertainty. An example of an assumption could be “assuming no change in budget,” or “assuming an operating environment consistent with typical local weather.” Goals, objectives, assumptions, and constraints may be available from current documentation or may need to be developed. Inputs Documented Criticality Analysis Procedures (or project plan) from Process A; Relevant Laws, Regulations, Directives (including organizational policies), and other high-level guiding documents that may have the right information; Strategic Plan(s); any documentation that describes organizational mission/vision; needs, goals, objectives, and projects; Risk Management Strategy (including risk tolerance); Budgets and Project Plan(s) Outputs Documentation of goals, objectives, assumptions, and constraints Methods Project Plan; Document Review; Brainstorming; Process Flow Diagram; Responsible/Accountable/Consulted/Informed (RACI) Charts.

If the high-level program workflow path is complex or the activities within the workflow are complex, separate the workflow into different processes or workflow paths (also known as “mission threads”). Each workflow path has an identifiable beginning and end. The more detail that is put into this representation, the more specific and tailored the overall criticality analysis can be. However, very detailed diagrams are also less flexible to changes and can be time-consuming to create; it is important to define what level of detail is necessary for the criticality analysis.5 Once the activities are identified and represented in a workflow or set of workflow paths, boundaries of those activities are defined and described, and individuals or entities who will be performing those activities identified. The boundaries and responsible individuals are documented in sufficient detail to provide enough information to identify which points in the process may be critical to the organization as analyzed in sub-processes B.4 and B.5, and Process E. Consider identifying the amount of control the organization has over certain dependencies (e.g., weather). Also, consider the individuals/responsibilities defined in B.2 and identify where multiple activities are conducted by a single individual or organizational unit. original_blocks.html: Sub-process ID B.4 Sub-process name Define Operating States Sub-process This sub-process describes regular operation of the program and what might description happen if the activities or workflow paths defined in B.2 are compromised. For each activity defined in B.2 and B.3, describe the condition of the activity (i.e., what the activity could look like) and the impact on the workflow if the activity is forced into different conditions, including but not limited to: Non-operational (i.e., the activity does not occur); Impaired (i.e., the activity operates at a reduced pace or in an unsafe/insecure/privacy-invasive manner); Normal operation (i.e., how the activity operates under typical or ideal circumstances); Increased operations (i.e., the activity performs quicker or with more output than normal); or Unintended operations (i.e., the activity performs but with additional outputs or actions that are not part of the expected routine).
original_blocks.extraction_note: 表の行列構造を要確認

original_blocks.html: Determine the severity of the operating states other than normal (adverse operating states) on the workflow. This could be a ranking (e.g., low, moderate, high) or measure (e.g., time lost; cost in time/resources). Consider defining what types of scenarios would lead to such situations. Examples of scenarios to consider include reduced performance (e.g., lower bandwidth), security breach, privacy problems, physical accident, or any other similar event (often described as an “adverse event” in security and privacy risk assessment models). Consider the time frame of an operating state– often long-term adverse operating states have greater impact than short-term states. Consider how long an adverse operating state must last before it becomes severe. Consider security, safety, and privacy ramifications. Examples of potential ramifications include (but are not limited to): determination of what information is made vulnerable if the activity is performed more slowly than expected, potential physical damages if an activity is performed too quickly, and privacy implications for personally identifiable information if unintended operations are performed. Also consider any contractual, statutory, or other obligations which may be impacted by the operating state. Then, using the Process Description and/or Diagram created in B.3, identify specific interactions, intersections, connections, and dependencies in the workflow paths that would be impacted by each adverse operating state. The purpose is to identify how the adverse operating states of the activity impact other activities in the process and in turn, which interactions or dependencies have the most influence on normal operation of the program and thus are more critical. original_blocks.html: System/Subsystem-Level Criticality Analysis. In the case of COTS products, the process will likely be performed out of sequence. Using the documentation and criticality levels developed in Process C along with any other relevant laws, regulations, directives, etc., identify which critical system/subsystem are to be further analyzed. For this portion of the criticality analysis, the system/subsystem is an IT/OT product, device, or solution, although the Model will support the analysis of any well-defined system. Separate analyses are conducted for all critical systems identified in Process C, if possible. This is because the components composing systems are often varied even if the systems seem identical. Ensure that the scope has definitive boundaries. Define any assumptions or constraints, which will help limit the analysis. Components and subcomponents are sometimes guided by specific legal and regulatory requirements, such as sourcing requirements (where those can/cannot come from); take those into account. If the analysis is conducted by a third party, such as in the case of COTS, work with the COTS provider(s) to define what information is available which may serve to inform a Baseline Criticality determination, including system documentation, risk analyses performed, operating constraints, and assumptions. If a system does not exist, but is being designed or is under development, bear in mind that the system design may change frequently. It may be best to perform this analysis from a theoretical viewpoint and use the result to inform the design and development process. Then repeat the process as changes to the design occur and when the system development has been completed. original_blocks.html: Sub-process ID D.2 Sub-process name Identify System Functions and Capabilities Workflow Needed and What Components/Subcomponents Will be Used Sub-process This sub-process analyzes the system to identify the components and description subcomponents required to ensure that the system functions as intended. Review the activities identified in D.1. For existing systems, list the functions and capabilities of the system being analyzed. For systems under development, list functions and capabilities needed. If the system is complex, consider scoping the analysis to only the functions and capabilities determined as critical. Consider configurations, settings, routines, performance parameters, etc. Define the processes or data actions that are activated or that the system uses to perform the identified functions and capabilities. Those processes can be extracted from existing system documentation, such as functional requirements, system diagrams, process flow diagrams, system concept of operations, or any other documentation that describes what the system does. Consider defining what information/data is needed to perform a function: how will that data be processed and how it will be secured. Finally, identify components and subcomponents that are or will be used to support required functionalities and capabilities. If possible, define all of the functions and capabilities of those components and subcomponents; identify which functions or capabilities are not needed or outside the requirements for this particular application. For example, configuration settings or functions that will not be used. Consider the frequency of use of subsystem functions and capabilities and describing end-of-life conditions, such as when the functions/capabilities are expected to no longer be needed, for the system to function. Inputs Determination of the system/subsystem from D.1; Existing documentation, system design process, architecture diagrams; existing contractual obligations Outputs Listing of capabilities and pathways needed to pass to D.3.

original_blocks.html: Sub-process ID D.3 Sub-process name Identify Interactions, Intersections, Connections, and Dependencies Within the System(s)/Subsystem(s) Sub-process This sub-process identifies interactions, intersections, connections, and description dependencies between components/subcomponents and associated functionalities/capabilities. The way the system uses components and subcomponents to execute a specific function or capability is described as a workflow path. Defined workflow paths may be extremely detailed, including the individual processes used by subcomponents. Note that detailed workflow paths allow for a more accurate and complete criticality analysis, but may not be feasible in many instances. Identify all workflow paths required to execute each system function or, if the system is complex, each critical function. In many cases, a single component, or identical components, will be used to support multiple workflow paths. Document these components matched to workflow paths in a matrix, spreadsheet, database, function diagram, or a similar tool. Identify interactions, intersections, connections, and dependencies between the components. Identify any constraints within the existing infrastructure. Consider identifying the amount of control the organization has over certain dependencies and constraints (e.g., weather). Consider defining triggers or conditions which activate/deactivate the use of a component or which impact how a component is used.

original_blocks.html: Sub-process ID D.4 Sub-process name Define Operating States Sub-process This sub-process defines normal operational states, as well as the states in description which the system will be operating abnormally. Review the outputs of D.3. Describe operation of the components and/or workflow paths. Then determine the impact of the various operating states of the component on the workflow path(s), and consequently on the system function/capability that path supports. Consider each of the following operating states: Non-operational; Impaired (i.e., the component/subcomponent operates at a reduced capability or in an unsafe/insecure/privacy-invasive manner); Normal operation; Increased operations (i.e., the function or capability performs quicker or with more output than normal); and Unintended operations (i.e., the function or capability performs but with additional outputs or actions that are not part of the expected routine).

original_blocks.html: Consider defining what types of scenarios would lead to such situations. Examples of scenarios to consider include reduced performance (e.g., lower bandwidth), security breach, physical accident, insertion of counterfeit part, or any other similar event. Using the Function Diagram with Workflow Paths, identify specific points within the workflow paths where the system will be particularly stressed as a result of any of these operating states. This would include any points that would exacerbate the situation. Define the severity of the impact of the operating states. This may be a ranking (e.g., low, moderate, high) or measure (e.g., processing speed; downtime; percentage of remaining functionality). Consider the security, safety, and privacy ramifications of these situations; for example, what information is made vulnerable if the components/subcomponents fail? Could the data processing create privacy problems for individuals? Also consider any contractual, statutory, or other obligations which may be impacted by the operating state. Consider the lifetime of the component/subcomponent and the duration of an adverse operating state. Often, the impact of an adverse operating state is more severe over a longer time frame.
